source.title: Sentiment Analysis and Language Models for Kwanyama

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports results bearing on repeated-data scaling and downstream performance with model size, but uses continued pretraining in a low-resource language rather than fitting the original scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al.; those cited findings are not extracted as results. It reports training-loss curves but does not quantify or fit power laws to held-out pretraining loss. The perplexity comparisons are across language domains and are not reported as a held-out pretraining-loss scaling fit. The repeated-data statement and the three O KA LM downstream accuracy results are extracted.
record.test_reason: A low-resource resource paper, not a scaling study. Its own results bear only weakly on V6: fine-tuned sentiment accuracy for three continued-pretrained sizes (1B/3B/8B). Its repeated-data remark is a one-sentence qualitative observation with no loss values. No power-law fit, extrapolation, allocation or shape sweep is run.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misweighted. The authors' conclusion is about introducing Kwanyama's first sentiment dataset and language models. The size trend (8B > 3B > 1B) is a side observation. The repeated-data remark is a passing anecdote attributed 'likely' to the small corpus, not a tested finding.
record.recipe_differences: Continued pretraining of LLaMA-3 checkpoints on a 6.58M-token Kwanyama corpus, generally for one epoch; the paper does not fit scaling laws or run an orders-of-magnitude sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that training beyond one epoch led to overfitting in their setting.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference (LREC 2026)
record.problems: The repeated-data result is qualitative, with no numerical loss or model-by-model breakdown. The downstream size trend covers only three models from 1B to 8B, and no uncertainty estimates or predictive fit are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results left out. The paper's training-loss curves and domain perplexity comparisons are not extracted as held-out pretraining-loss power-law results.

untested.parts: No power-law fit; only three sizes within one order of magnitude; training loss curves and domain perplexities not fitted.
No measured repeated-data loss curve, epoch sweep or fit; other modalities and regimes untested.
Predictability (curve fit, relation to pretraining loss) untested; only three sizes, one task.

missing.what: Perplexity of OkaLM-1B/3B/8B (and untuned LLaMA-3 bases) on four held-out Kwanyama domains. 8B is lowest overall; values are garbled in the extracted text. This is held-out loss versus size, but only three sizes, so it cannot test a power law.
missing.versions: V1 (weak, cannot establish power law), V6

record.verdict_notes: The study is not one of the originals. No V5 verdict is given because r1 has no measurable outcome and is from a continued-pretraining regime far outside where repeated-data laws were fitted. Muennighoff et al. themselves predict rapidly vanishing returns at such repetition levels, so the remark need not contradict them. Downstream sizes come from different LLaMA-3 checkpoints (3.2 1B/3B vs 3 8B), so the trend reflects base-model scale as well as continued pretraining.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining-loss power-law fit or orders-of-magnitude parameter, token, or compute sweep.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run losses.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architectures at fixed parameter count.
The paper reports only its repeated-data setting; it does not test other modalities, fine-tuning and transfer regimes generally, or repeated-data scaling across multiple data and compute scales.
Tests sentiment classification on O KA S ENTIMENT for three O KA LM sizes; other downstream tasks and predictive fits against pretraining loss are not tested.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or curve shapes.

rows.subject: O KA LM models (1B, 3B, and 8B; aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: Trained beyond the reported one-epoch regime on the Kwanyama corpus.
rows.value: The authors state that repeated-data scaling laws did not hold in their setting and that training beyond one epoch led to overfitting.
rows.note: The paper gives this as an aggregate result for its setting; it does not report separate outcomes by model size or a numerical loss.
rows.check: Qualitative remark only ('training beyond one epoch led to overfitting'), with no held-out loss, epoch count or per-size values. The setting is continued pretraining of 1–8B models on 6.58M tokens, an extreme repetition regime, so it cannot show whether a repeated-data power law holds or fails. 'reversed' is not supported by any number.

rows.subject: O KA LM-1B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on the O KA S ENTIMENT training set and evaluated for sentiment classification.
rows.note: The reported result is part of a three-size monotonic accuracy trend, but the study does not fit or validate a predictive scaling curve.
rows.check: 55% is the low point of a monotonic three-size trend; it is observed for 'improves with scale'. Predictability is not tested (no fit). Base checkpoints differ by size (LLaMA-3 family), so scale is the only varied factor named, but there is no uncertainty and n=300 test items.

rows.subject: O KA LM-3B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on the O KA S ENTIMENT training set and evaluated for sentiment classification.
rows.note: The reported result is part of a three-size monotonic accuracy trend, but the study does not fit or validate a predictive scaling curve.
rows.check: 62%, between 1B and 8B, consistent with monotonic improvement; no fit or uncertainty.

rows.subject: O KA LM-8B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on the O KA S ENTIMENT training set and evaluated for sentiment classification.
rows.note: The reported result is part of a three-size monotonic accuracy trend, but the study does not fit or validate a predictive scaling curve.
rows.check: 70%, highest of the three sizes; no fit or uncertainty.

relationships.condition: OkaLM 1B/3B/8B fine-tuned on OkaSentiment, 300-review test set
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises monotonically with size (55%, 62%, 70%; r2–r4). This is only directional, with no predictive fit or uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: Sentiment accuracy increased monotonically from 55% to 62% to 70% across the tested model sizes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
